newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Q1 company results show general decline.
newsitem.headline: Thai Q1 company results show general decline.

text.p: A deluge of first quarter results from Thai firms on Friday showed a general decline in earnings but most were above worst case expectations, analysts said.
With most finance firms and bank results out last month, attention focused on results from Thailand's industrial, property, construction, communications and chemical sectors.

"Most results are out and were quite in line with our expectations which were bad. There were very few surprises as we had pretty low expectations," Tom Paiboon, head of research at TISCO, told Reuters.

Thailand's slowing growth rate, widely forecast at a decade low of between 5-6 percent this year and high interest rates at a minimum 12.75 percent, have lowered domestic demand for goods and raised corporate financing costs, analysts said.

"Across the board the results so far show a decline ... that may indicate it will be hard to get GDP growth to reach 5-6 percent forecasts this year," said Chinda Petchployngamee, head of resercah at Thai Rung Reung.

A weaker baht against the dollar in the first quarter had also taken its toll on firms heavily reliant on unhedged U.S. dollar financing, although the extent to which the weakening affected earnings was hard to determine without further study, analysts said.

"My first impression is that it's not as bad as it could have been, though telecoms seems to be blowing up and the fixed-line operators are up against the wall," said a senior analyst at Krungthai Thanakit.

The huge investment costs of installing fixed-lines and lower than projected take-up rates given slower growth and a construction slowdown hammered TelecomAsia's earnings, analysts said. The firm posted a 439 million baht ($16.88 million) loss against a small profit last year.
Chemical companies, heavy U.S.dollar borrowers for capital intensive investments in the last few years, posted mixed results but did offer some pleasant surprises, analysts said.
"Some people like NPC did a little better than expected though in the longer term we expect an oversupply situation to affect the sector," Paiboon said.

Energy results from power producer Cogeneration Plc and coal firm Banpu Plc were in line though losses at state-backed privatisation candidate Bangchak Petroleum Plc's came as a surprise, said an analyst at National Finance and Securities.
Cogeneration posted a slightly higher first quarter profit of 187.73 million baht versus 152.07 million in the corresponding 1996 quarter.
Bangchak posted a loss of 91.23 million baht against a profit of 377.23 million in the same period.
"I was very surprised Bangchak reported a loss," he said, attributing the decline to a possible fall in margins from refining operations.

Among constructors Ch Karnchang's backlog of expressway work remains a solid revenue earner for the firm, though the overall picture for the industry in a year of government budget cuts remains poor, analysts said.
Its first quarter net rose to 165.55 million baht versus 149.25 million baht previously.

The country's largest constructor Italian-Thai Development Plc posted a 25.4 percent fall in first quarter earnings. ITD's first quarter net fell to 394.61 million baht against 528.69 million baht previously.

Declining earnings of leading firms in the oversupplied property sector were widely anticipated. Land and House Plc MBK Properties Plc and Central Pattana Plc all reported sharp falls in first quarter profits.
"The issue for property firms is not so much profits at the moment as cash flow," Paiboon said.
